st.1: Banawali (about 550 ha) shows unbroken occupation from the Early to the Mature Harappan phase.

x: Neither statement is correct: the 550-ha site with unbroken Early-to-Mature occupation is Rakhigarhi, not Banawali; Tighrana and Mitathal are in Bhiwani district, not Hisar.

st.1: The copper scale was found at Harappa.

x: All three statements are correct: the copper scale is from Harappa, the ivory scale (smallest division ~1.70 mm) from Lothal and the shell scale (~6.7 mm) from Mohenjodaro.

st.3: Temples have been found in Harappan cities, though no royal palaces.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: the Great Bath and the pillared hall were public buildings, not royal palaces; neither royal palaces nor temples have been found in Harappan cities.

st.2: The Priest-King was found at Mohenjodaro.

x: All three statements are correct: the red sandstone male torso is from Harappa, while the steatite Priest-King bust was found at Mohenjodaro.

st.2: A fire altar has also been found at Lothal in Rajasthan.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: Lothal, which has a fire altar, is in Gujarat, not Rajasthan; the terracotta cake with the horned deity and the goat is from Kalibangan, not Banawali.

st.3: The term Vaishya derives from Jana.
st.1: The family was patriarchal, patrilineal and matrilocal.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: the family was patrilocal, not matrilocal; Vaishya derives from Vis, not Jana; the units in ascending order were Kula – Grama – Vis – Jana.

st.1: The Avadanashataka is written in Pali.
st.3: The Vinayavatthu, a Jain text, mentions the 'Andhrapatha'.

x: Only statement 4 is correct: the Avadanashataka is in Sanskrit, not Pali; the Mahavamsa was written by Mahanama, not Ashvaghosha; the Vinayavatthu is a Buddhist (Vinaya) text, not a Jain one.

st.3: The first human images of the Buddha were made in the Kushana period at Mathura and Gandhara.

x: All three statements are correct: Hinayana showed the Buddha by symbols, and Mahayana adopted images, first made in the Kushana period at Mathura and Gandhara.

st.2: The Buddhist doctrine of anatta agrees with the Jain belief in an eternal soul (jiva) in all things.
st.1: Buddhism follows a stricter ahimsa, extending even to thought, while Jainism follows the Middle Way.

x: Only statement 4 is correct: it is Jainism that follows the stricter ahimsa and Buddhism the Middle Way; anatta contrasts with, not agrees with, the Jain jiva; both religions accept karma and rebirth.

st.3: Jain writers enriched Prakrit, Apabhramsa and Kannada, but never wrote in Telugu.
st.1: The early Jains discarded Prakrit and preached in Sanskrit.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: the early Jains discarded Sanskrit and preached in Prakrit; Jain writers enriched Telugu too, along with Prakrit, Apabhramsa and Kannada; Kundakundacharya's Saraswati gachcha was at Konakondla, not Ramatirtham.

st.3: The fragments were compiled by Schwanbeck in 1846.

x: All three statements are correct: Megasthenes was Seleucus I's envoy at Pataliputra, and the lost Indica survives in fragments compiled by Schwanbeck in 1846.

st.2: Kautilya's saying 'a chariot cannot move on one wheel' stresses the king's need for a strong army.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: the saying stresses the king's need for ministers, not an army; the Mauryas did not issue gold coins – their currency was punch-marked silver.

st.3: These edicts are in the Prakrit language and the Brahmi script.

x: All three statements are correct: Erragudi has the 14 Major Rock Edicts and a Minor Rock Edict, Rajula Mandagiri only a Minor Rock Edict, both in Prakrit and Brahmi.

st.4: The suvarna was a gold coin in common use.
st.3: The kakani was a copper coin worth four times a mashaka.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: the mashaka was a copper coin, not gold; the kakani was worth one-fourth of a mashaka, not four times; the gold suvarna was not in common use.

st.2: Agra was founded by the Lodis.

x: All three statements are correct: token currency and the transfer of the capital belong to the Tughlaqs, Agra was founded by the Lodis (Sikandar Lodi), and the Lodis were the first Afghan dynasty.

st.3: State granaries were kept sealed and never released grain, even in times of shortage.
st.4: Soldiers of the royal army were used to make test purchases.
st.1: Its plan aimed at free-market prices, sure supply, controlled distribution and the end of monopolies.

x: None of the statements is correct: the plan aimed at fixed, not free-market, prices; its aim was to pay a large army low wages, not the palace artisans; state granaries released grain in times of shortage; slave boys, not soldiers, made the test purchases.

st.3: Balban told Qazi Mughisuddin that he ordered whatever was good for the state.
st.4: Firoz Shah Tughlaq leaned on the Sufis against the ulema and visited the Ajmer shrine.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: Hindu gods were worshipped in the palace in 1320 under Nasiruddin Khusrau Shah, not Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah; it was Alauddin Khalji, not Balban, who told Qazi Mughisuddin this; it was Muhammad bin Tughlaq, not Firoz Shah, who leaned on the Sufis and visited Ajmer.

st.1: It was dedicated to Ibrahim Adil Shah of Bijapur.

x: All three statements are correct: Firishta dedicated his history to Ibrahim Adil Shah of Bijapur, called Telangana 'Tilang', and his Deva Raya–Nehal story is rejected by modern historians.

st.3: Iltutmish's tomb has the first true arch.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct: the double dome was pioneered by the Lodis but reached the Mughals through Humayun's Tomb, not Akbar's; the first true arch is in Balban's tomb, not Iltutmish's.

st.1: He was a contemporary of the Kakatiya king Prataparudra II.

x: Neither statement is correct: Annamacharya (1408–1503) was a contemporary of Saluva Narasimha, not of Prataparudra II (died 1323); nor was he a contemporary of Tyagaraja (1767–1847).

st.1: The papal bull Inter caetera (1493) was issued by Pope Nicholas V.
st.2: The Treaty of Tordesillas (1494) drew the dividing line 370 leagues east of Cape Verde.

x: None of the statements is correct: Inter caetera was issued by Alexander VI, not Nicholas V; the line was 370 leagues west of Cape Verde, not east; lands east of the line went to Portugal, not Spain.

st.2: Lord Dalhousie was not the originator of the doctrine; states had been taken on this ground before him.

x: All three statements are correct: a dependent state without a natural male heir lapsed to the Company; the doctrine predated Dalhousie, who announced and first systematically applied it in 1848.

st.2: The real start of the revolt was the rising at Meerut on 10 May 1857.

x: All three statements are correct: Canning was Governor-General, the revolt really began at Meerut on 10 May 1857, and the rebels at Delhi killed Commissioner Simon Fraser.

st.4: Tantia Tope was hanged at Gwalior.
st.1: Kunwar Singh died at Jagdishpur on 26 April 1857.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: Kunwar Singh died at Jagdishpur on 26 April 1858, not 1857; Havelock died at Lucknow, not Delhi; Tantia Tope was hanged at Shivpuri, not Gwalior.

st.2: Under it Madras was returned to the English in exchange for Quebec in North America.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: Madras was returned in exchange for Louisbourg, not Quebec; the Second Carnatic War ended with the Treaty of Pondicherry (1754-55), not the Treaty of Paris.

st.2: Both Companies retained the right to interfere in the quarrels of Indian princes.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: both Companies agreed not to interfere in Indian princes' quarrels; Muhammad Ali, not Chanda Sahib, was recognised as Nawab of the Carnatic.

st.4: The Kol rising led by Buddho Bhagat took place in 1855-56.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the Pabna movement (1873) was in Bengal, not Bihar; Buddho Bhagat's Kol rising was in 1831-32, not 1855-56 (the Santhal rising).

st.1: Per capita income was about Rs 20.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct: per capita income on the eve of independence was about Rs 265 (Rs 20 is the 1867-68 estimate); agriculture gave about 50 per cent of GDP, not 30.

st.1: The Press and Registration of Periodicals Act, 2023 replaced the Act of 1878.
st.4: India was ranked 157th of 180 in the World Press Freedom Index 2026 released by UNESCO.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: the 2023 Act replaced the Act of 1867, not 1878; the Press Council (1978 Act) has no punitive powers; the World Press Freedom Index is released by Reporters Without Borders (RSF), not UNESCO.

st.3: Kesari was founded by Bal Gangadhar Tilak in 1881.

x: All three statements are correct: Som Prakash was Vidyasagar's idea with Dwarkanath Vidyabhushan as editor, The Bengalee passed to Surendranath Banerjea in 1879, and Tilak founded Kesari in 1881.

st.4: He worked with Periyar E.V. Ramasamy among the Malas.
st.2: That conference took the name Adi-Dravida Mahajana Sabha.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: the conference took the name Adi-Andhra, not Adi-Dravida, Mahajana Sabha; the title 'Varma' came from the Arya Samaj, not the Brahmo Samaj; he worked with Arige Ramaswamy, not Periyar, among the Malas.

st.1: Ambedkar rejected the view that caste is merely a division of labour, calling it a division of labourers.

x: All three statements are correct: Ambedkar called caste a division of labourers, not merely of labour, traced its sanction to the Shastras and saw inter-caste marriage as the real remedy.

st.3: The annual Congress session lasted only about three days, with a permanent secretariat working between sessions.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: the Moderates never organised mass civil disobedience; the three-day annual session had no machinery working between sessions.

st.3: Bhagat Singh threw the bombs along with Batukeshwar Dutt.

x: All three statements are correct: the bombs protested the Public Safety and Trade Disputes Bills, the leaflet spoke of making 'the deaf hear', and Bhagat Singh threw them with Batukeshwar Dutt.

st.1: The Tinkathia system (indigo on 3/20 of the land) belongs to Kheda (1918).

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct: Tinkathia belongs to Champaran (1917), not Kheda; the Pabna movement led to the Bengal Tenancy Act, 1885 – the Deccan Agriculturists' Relief Act (1879) followed the Deccan riots.

st.4: The Commission arrived at Calcutta on 3 February 1928, greeted by an all-India hartal.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: the Justice Party did not join the boycott, though the Hindu Mahasabha did; the Commission arrived at Bombay, not Calcutta, on 3 February 1928.

st.2: Champaran Satyagraha
st.1: Report of the Hunter Committee

x: Not a statement set (chronology): the correct order is 2-4-3-1 – Champaran Satyagraha (1917), Rowlatt Satyagraha hartal (April 1919), Amritsar session of the Congress (December 1919), Hunter Committee report (1920).

st.3: The crowd at Jallianwala Bagh was protesting the arrest of Kitchlew and Satyapal and was fired upon only after a warning to disperse.
st.4: Michael O'Dwyer was the Lt. Governor of Punjab, and the House of Commons backed Dyer.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: the Satyagraha Sabha was formed at Bombay, not Ahmedabad; the crowd was fired upon without any warning; it was the House of Lords, not the Commons, that backed Dyer.

st.1: Dandi is a coastal village in Navsari district of Gujarat.

x: All three statements are correct: Dandi is in Navsari district; the march covered about 240 miles in 24 days on foot and reached Dandi on 5 April 1930.

st.2: The Quit India Movement began in 1942.

x: All three statements are correct: Non-Cooperation began in 1920, Civil Disobedience in 1930 and Quit India in 1942.

st.4: Subhas Chandra Bose
st.1: Mahatma Gandhi

x: Not a statement set (matching): A-3, B-2, C-1, D-4 – 'Netaji' from the people of Germany, 'Desh Nayak' from Tagore, 'Prince among Patriots' from Gandhi, and Bose called Gandhi 'Father of the Nation'.

st.4: Gandhi called Mandalay Jail his "Mandir".

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct: Tolstoy Farm was named after Tolstoy by Hermann Kallenbach, not by Gandhi; the jail Gandhi called his 'Mandir' was Yerawada (Pune), not Mandalay.

st.2: Wrote the song 'Paradesiyulu tolagandi...'
st.4: Wrote the diary 'Feathers and Stones'

x: Not a statement set (matching): A-3, B-2, C-1, D-4 – Nivarthy Venkata Subbaiah stayed underground, Vanamamalai Varadacharyulu wrote 'Paradesiyulu tolagandi', Mamidipudi Venkatarangayya moved the Andhra University resolution, and Pattabhi wrote 'Feathers and Stones'.

st.1: Patel warned Nehru about China after Tibet in a letter of 7 November 1950.

x: All three statements are correct: Patel's China letter was of 7 November 1950; Nehru took Kashmir to the UN while Patel favoured military action, as he did on Hyderabad (Operation Polo, 1948).

st.1: The Janmabhoomi programme was launched under Chief Minister N.T. Rama Rao.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: Janmabhoomi (1997) was launched under Chandrababu Naidu, not NTR; Rajiv Aarogyasri (2007) was launched under Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy, not NTR.

st.1: P. Anandacharlu, the first Telugu President of the INC, presided over the Madras session of 1891.
st.2: Pattabhi Sitaramayya lost the Tripuri (1939) contest to Nehru and became President at Jaipur in 1948.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: Anandacharlu presided over the Nagpur session of 1891, not a Madras one; Pattabhi lost the 1939 contest to Bose, not Nehru; the Kakinada session of 1923 was presided over by Maulana Mohammad Ali, not Pattabhi.

st.1: It was introduced in Andhra Pradesh on 2 October 1959.
st.3: It was introduced when Damodaram Sanjivayya was Chief Minister.

x: None of the statements is correct: Panchayat Raj came to AP on 1 November 1959 (2 October 1959 is Rajasthan's date); Rajasthan was first, AP second; the Chief Minister was Neelam Sanjiva Reddy, not Damodaram Sanjivayya.

st.3: The agitation was called off on 1 October 1973, after the 32nd Amendment had been passed.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the agitation was called off on 1 October 1973 after the Six-Point Formula, before the 32nd Amendment (December 1973); Jalagam Vengala Rao, not Kasu Brahmananda Reddy, became CM when President's Rule ended.

st.2: T.V. Mahalingam held that Simhavarman, as a crowned king, completed the Pallava takeover.
st.1: D.C. Sircar held that Pallava Simhavarman helped bring down the Ikshvakus in the 6th century CE.

x: Neither statement is correct: Sircar placed Simhavarman's role at the end of the 3rd century CE, not the 6th; Mahalingam held that Simhavarman bore no royal title and that Sivaskandavarman I completed the takeover.

st.3: Cross-cousin marriage in Andhra began with the Vishnukundins, who also allied with the Kshatrapas of Ujjain and the Chutus.
st.1: Brahmins formed the majority.

x: Only statement 4 is correct: Shudras, not Brahmins, formed the majority; Brahmadeya grants were exempt from 18 taxes, not 12; cross-cousin marriage and the Kshatrapa–Chutu alliances belong to the Ikshvakus, not the Vishnukundins.

st.2: A Roman-style amphitheatre has been found at Vijayapuri (Nagarjunakonda).

x: All three statements are correct: Roman trade was lower than under the Satavahanas, a Roman-style amphitheatre stands at Vijayapuri, and spices, iron, coconuts and cotton went out while wine and glassware came in.

st.2: The Ramatirtham plates record his marriage to a daughter of the Vakataka Prithvisena II.
st.1: He performed 16 Ashvamedhas, 11 Rajasuyas and one Purushamedha.

x: Only statement 4 is correct: he performed 11 Ashvamedhas and 16 Rajasuyas, not the reverse; the marriage is recorded in the Khanapur plates, not the Ramatirtham plates; he took Karma-rashtra from the Pallavas, not the Anandagotrikas.

st.3: Before 575 CE Telugu appears in records in full prose sentences.
st.4: Between 575 and 848 CE Telugu appears in metrical verse.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: the Renati Cholas did so about five centuries, not three, before Nannaya; before 575 CE Telugu appears only in names; between 575 and 848 CE it appears in prose sentences, not verse.

st.2: Madanavilasabanam was written by Srinatha at Anavota's court, not by Naganatha.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct: Sringara Naishadham is based on Sriharsha's Naishadhiyacharita, not the Raghuvamsa; Madanavilasabanam is by Naganatha, not Srinatha.

st.3: It was originally a Kakatiya fort, rebuilt by Sultan Quli and Ibrahim Qutb Shah.

x: All three statements are correct: Golconda (old name Mankal) was a Kakatiya fort rebuilt by Sultan Quli and Ibrahim, and a handclap at its gate carries to the Bala Hisar.

st.3: Kaadarambamu (Metta, dry) land paid its tax in cash at a lower rate than irrigated land.

x: All three statements are correct: revenue was usually 1/6 (1/4 or 1/3 on fertile land), the documents were Adhuvanatantram, and dry Metta land paid in cash at a lower rate than irrigated Magani land.

st.4: Domingo Paes called the sacked city a 'graveyard'.
st.1: H.K. Sherwani calls it the battle of Rakshasa-Tangadi.
st.3: Hampi was looted for about six weeks.

x: None of the statements is correct: Sherwani calls it the battle of Bannihatti, not Rakshasa-Tangadi; Sadasiva and Tirumala fled to Penukonda, not Chandragiri; Hampi was looted for about six months, not weeks; the 'graveyard' remark is Robert Sewell's, not Domingo Paes's.

st.1: Krishnadevaraya allowed a church at Chandragiri.

x: Neither statement is correct: the church at Chandragiri was allowed by Venkatapati Raya II, not Krishnadevaraya; Venkatapati Raya II belonged to the Aravidu, not the Tuluva, dynasty.

st.3: The Kakatiya Kala Thoranam – four ornate stone gateways around the Swayambhu Shiva temple – is in the Andhra Pradesh State emblem.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the Kala Thoranam is in the Telangana, not the Andhra Pradesh, emblem; the gateways were built by the Kakatiyas, not by Ulugh Khan.

st.1: It was started at Madras on 15 August 1938 by The Hindu group.

x: Neither statement is correct: Andhra Prabha was started by the Indian Express group (Ramnath Goenka), not The Hindu group; its noted editor was Narla Venkateswara Rao, not Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao.

st.2: Gadaba belongs to the Munda family.

x: All three statements are correct: Savara and Gadaba belong to the Munda family, and Savara is the only AP tribal language with its own script.

st.2: The Muralidhar Rao Commission took charge on 27 January 1982.

x: All three statements are correct: the Anantharaman Commission (1968–70) grouped BCs into A–D, and the Muralidhar Rao Commission took charge on 27 January 1982 and put the combined share at 29.08%.

st.2: The Mandal Commission was set up on 1 January 1979 by the Indira Gandhi government and reported on 31 December 1980.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct: the Mandal Commission was set up by the Morarji Desai (Janata) government, not Indira Gandhi's; its recommendations were implemented on 7 August 1990 by the V.P. Singh government, not Rajiv Gandhi's.

st.2: It was founded in Surabhi village of Kadapa district.

x: All three statements are correct: the Surabhi company was founded in 1885 in Surabhi village of Kadapa district by Vanarasa Govinda Rao and his brother.

st.2: The Lalit Kala Akademi was set up in 1961.

x: Neither statement is correct: the Sahitya Akademi is a registered society, not a statutory body; the Lalit Kala Akademi was set up in 1954, not 1961.

st.3: Dalit Mahasabhas were formed after the Karamchedu incident of 1985.

x: All three statements are correct: Chikkanavutunna Pata appeared in 1995, Padunekkina Pata in 1996, and Dalit Mahasabhas followed the Karamchedu incident of 1985.

st.2: The TDP's founding slogan was 'Jai Andhra'.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct: the TDP's founding slogan was 'Telugu Vari Atma Gauravam', not 'Jai Andhra'; the 1993 arrack ban came under Kotla Vijaya Bhaskara Reddy, not N. Janardhana Reddy.

st.1: Vaishali, capital of the Shakya republic, was named after King Vishal.
st.3: Kumrahar and Bulandibagh are excavated remains of Rajgriha.
st.4: Pava was the place of Mahavira's first sermon.

x: None of the statements is correct: Vaishali was the capital of the Lichchhavis, not the Shakyas; the First Council met at Rajagriha (Vaishali hosted the Second); Kumrahar and Bulandibagh are remains of Pataliputra, not Rajgriha; Mahavira's first sermon was at Rajgriha – Pava is where he died.

st.2: The sculptor Mallitamma is associated with Konark.
st.3: The Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas were inscribed on the UNESCO list in 2021.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: Mallitamma is associated with Somanathapura, not Konark; the Hoysala ensembles were inscribed in 2023, not 2021 (Ramappa's year); Ramappa is a separate World Heritage Site, not part of the Hoysala ensembles.

st.1: Ramanujacharya sent priests from southern temples to the north and vice versa.
st.3: Linguistic reorganisation acted as a "safety valve" and made India a "Nation-State".
st.4: Kerala (1956) was the first linguistic State.

x: None of the statements is correct: it was Shankaracharya, not Ramanuja, who exchanged priests between south and north; linguistic homogeneity is not a bond of unity; reorganisation made India a 'State-Nation', not a 'Nation-State'; Andhra (1953), not Kerala, was the first linguistic State.

st.4: The RTE Act, 2009 came into force in 2010 under Article 45.
st.1: Urbanisation turns the family into a production unit.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: urbanisation makes the family a consumption, not production, unit; it increases social distance; the RTE Act rests on Article 21A, not Article 45.

st.1: The rise of single-parent and female-headed households is due mainly to widowhood, marital instability and male migration.

x: All three statements are correct: single-parent and female-headed homes rise with widowhood, marital instability and male migration, and Oommen found joint families with strong elder-male authority in the proprietary class.

st.1: A Christian convert can claim Scheduled Caste status merely on the basis of earlier caste identity.

x: Neither statement is correct: a Christian convert cannot claim SC status merely on earlier caste identity; ST status does not depend on the religion professed.

st.3: The 52nd Amendment (1985) deals with the lowering of the voting age.
st.1: The Religious Institutions (Prevention of Misuse) Act, 1988 allows religious premises to be used for political activity.

x: None of the statements is correct: the 1988 Act bars, not allows, political use of religious premises; freedom of religion is in Articles 25-28, while 29-30 cover cultural and educational rights; the 52nd Amendment dealt with anti-defection – the voting age was lowered by the 61st.

st.3: According to that survey, after alcohol the most-used substance was cannabis, followed by opioids.

x: All three statements are correct: India lies between the Golden Crescent and the Golden Triangle; the 2019 MoSJE–AIIMS-NDDTC survey found alcohol, then cannabis, then opioids most used.

st.1: The POCSO (Amendment) Act, 2019 prescribes a minimum of 20 years for aggravated penetrative sexual assault, extendable to life imprisonment but not death.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct: the 2019 amendment allows even death for aggravated penetrative sexual assault; the April 2018 Ordinance targeted rape of girls below 12 years, not 16.

st.1: The Central Social Welfare Board was set up in 1959.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: the Central Social Welfare Board was set up in 1953, not 1959; the shift from welfare to development for women came in the Sixth Plan, not the Fifth.

st.2: It held that gender identity is a matter of self-identification, not biological examination.

x: All three statements are correct: NALSA (15 April 2014, Radhakrishnan and Sikri JJ.) recognised self-identified gender, not biological tests, and directed separate toilets and health facilities.

st.4: Registered workers get a 16-digit UAN.
st.1: It was launched on 26 August 2021 by the Ministry of Rural Development.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: e-Shram was launched by the Ministry of Labour and Employment, not Rural Development; workers aged 16-59, not 18-60, can register; they get a 12-digit, not 16-digit, UAN.

st.3: Prison manuals are to be revised in line with the RPwD Act, 2016.

x: All three statements are correct: safe footpaths (min. 1.8 m) and digital access are part of Article 21, and prison manuals are to be revised in line with the RPwD Act, 2016.

st.1: It rests on separation of powers between the legislature and the executive, whereas the presidential form rests on co-operation and co-ordination.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: the parliamentary form rests on co-operation between legislature and executive and the presidential form on separation of powers, not the reverse; the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha, not the Rajya Sabha.

st.2: The restricted franchise used to elect it came from the Government of India Act, 1935.

x: All three statements are correct: the League won 73 seats, the provincial assemblies were elected on the restricted franchise of the 1935 Act, and princely States' members were nominated by their rulers.

st.2: The Indian Union is not the result of an agreement among the States.

x: All three statements are correct: Article 1 calls India a Union of States, the Union is not the result of an agreement among the States, and no State may secede.

st.3: Deprivation does not apply to citizens by birth.

x: All three statements are correct: minors of a renouncing parent may resume citizenship within a year of majority, a naturalised citizen jailed for two years within five years may be deprived, and deprivation does not apply to citizens by birth.

st.2: The term is not defined anywhere in the Constitution.

x: All three statements are correct: before 1976 'secular' appeared only in Article 25(2)(a), it is defined nowhere in the Constitution, and in India it means equal respect for all religions.

st.2: Article 13(1) applies to pre-constitutional laws, i.e. laws in force before the commencement of the Constitution.

x: All three statements are correct: Article 13(4) (24th Amendment) excludes Article 368 amendments, 13(1) covers pre-constitutional laws, and 'law' includes custom or usage.

st.3: A.K. Gopalan held that Article 21 protects only against arbitrary executive action, not legislative action.

x: All three statements are correct: Gopalan read Articles 19, 21 and 22 separately and protected only against executive action, while Maneka Gandhi required a just, fair and reasonable procedure.

st.3: Joseph Shine (2018) relied on constitutional morality only.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: NCT Delhi (2018) relied on constitutional morality only, not transformative constitutionalism; Joseph Shine (2018) relied on transformative constitutionalism only, not constitutional morality.

st.1: The 87th Amendment, 2003 provided for readjustment of constituencies on the basis of the 1991 Census.

x: Neither statement is correct: the 87th Amendment based readjustment on the 2001 Census, not 1991; the 2002 Delimitation Commission was chaired by Justice Kuldip Singh, not Kuldip Nayar.

st.3: Ministers cannot be elected to the financial committees.

x: All three statements are correct: all 30 Estimates Committee members are from the Lok Sabha, the PAC has 22 members, and Ministers are ineligible for the financial committees.

st.3: Such an extension may continue for up to one year after the Emergency has ceased to operate.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: Parliament may extend the term one year, not two years, at a time; the extension cannot continue beyond six months after the Emergency ends.

st.1: In a hung Assembly, the Sarkaria-Punchhi order gives the first preference to a pre-poll alliance.

x: All three statements are correct: the Sarkaria-Punchhi order puts a pre-poll alliance first; in Tamil Nadu (May 2026) Vijay was invited on 120 letters with an early floor test; the Kurian Joseph Committee proposed a new Schedule on the Governor's discretion.

st.2: Under Article 258A, the Governor entrusts State functions to the Union without the Centre's consent.
st.1: Under Article 258(2), Parliament may entrust functions to a State only with the State's consent.

x: Neither statement is correct: under Article 258(2) Parliament can confer functions on a State even without its consent; under Article 258A the Governor entrusts State functions to the Union only with the Centre's consent.

st.3: Under Article 320 the UPSC conducts examinations for All-India, Central and State services.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: posts are excluded from UPSC consultation by regulations made by the President, not Parliament; the UPSC conducts examinations for All-India and Central services, not State services, which belong to the State PSCs.

st.1: Reports on the accounts of a State are submitted to the President under Article 151(2).
st.2: Union reports go to the Lok Sabha Speaker, who causes them to be laid before Parliament, after which the Public Accounts Committee examines them.

x: Only statement 4 is correct: State reports go to the Governor, not the President; Union reports go to the President, not the Speaker; reports on public undertakings are examined by the Committee on Public Undertakings, not the Estimates Committee.

st.2: Its headquarters is at Amaravati.
st.4: In the Gade Sai Krishna custodial death (June 2026), the Supreme Court sought reports from the AP SHRC, the DGP and the Chief Secretary.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: the AP SHRC's headquarters is at Kurnool, not Amaravati; it has been without a chairperson since March 2024; it was the NHRC, not the Supreme Court, that sought the reports in the Gade Sai Krishna case.

st.2: In June 2013 the CIC declared six national parties public authorities, but the parties did not comply.

x: All three statements are correct: the 2013 Amendment Bill lapsed, the parties ignored the CIC's June 2013 order, and RTI coverage aims to check corruption, cronyism and illegal foreign funds.

st.2: It did not recommend abolition of the All India Services; it recommended strengthening them.

x: All three statements are correct: the Sarkaria Commission (June 1983, report 1988) wanted the All India Services strengthened (abolition was Rajamannar's idea) and residuary taxation left with Parliament.

st.1: Cesses are criticised because they are not shared with the States.

x: All three statements are correct: cesses are not shared with the States, the Planning Commission was an extra-constitutional body that made States aid-dependent, and Articles 256, 257, 356 and 365 are seen as tools of Union overreach.

st.2: Strictly, the first formal multi-party coalition at the Centre was the National Front of 1989.

x: All three statements are correct: Janata (1977) formed the first non-Congress government, the first formal coalition was the National Front (1989), and PEPSU's United Front (1952) preceded Kerala's CPI ministry (1957).

st.1: Action was taken at once at the Central level by the Janata government.
st.2: Karnataka, West Bengal and Andhra Pradesh acted on it, creating 'first generation panchayats'.
st.3: West Bengal held panchayat polls on its lines in June 1978 under its Act of 1983.

x: None of the statements is correct: no central action followed because the Janata government fell; the States created 'second generation', not 'first generation', panchayats; West Bengal's June 1978 polls were under its Act of 1973, not 1983; the Sixth Plan, not the Seventh, gave PRIs new life.

st.2: PSU assets were undervalued and disinvestment proceeds went mainly into new capital investment.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: disinvestment proceeds were used to plug revenue gaps, not for new capital investment; public investment in agriculture fell, not rose, after 1991.

st.3: The theme of the 28th NCeG was 'Viksit Bharat: Civil Service & Digital Transformation'.

x: All three statements are correct: the Jaipur Declaration (29th) covered DPI, AI, cybersecurity and data governance; the Visakhapatnam Declaration (28th) sought NeSDA for low-connectivity areas under the theme 'Viksit Bharat: Civil Service & Digital Transformation'.

st.4: Under the 2026 Amendment Rules, the prior price shown must be the highest in the preceding 30 days.
st.2: The grievance officer must acknowledge a complaint within 48 hours and redress it within three months.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: an entity that owns the goods is an inventory entity, not a marketplace; complaints must be redressed within one month, not three; the prior price must be the lowest, not the highest, in the preceding 30 days.

st.1: Srikakulam had the highest forest cover among the old districts.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct: the highest forest cover was in Visakhapatnam, not Srikakulam; the largest forest area was in YSR Kadapa, not East Godavari.

st.4: As per ISFR 2021, Andhra Pradesh ranks first in Recorded Forest Area with 37,258 sq km.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct: the ISFR is published every two years, not annually; AP ranks 8th, not first, in Recorded Forest Area – Madhya Pradesh is first.

st.2: Andhra Pradesh's median age of 32.5 is the highest among all Indian States.
st.4: By 2036 its 60+ share is projected to fall to about 10%.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: AP's median age of 32.5 (India 28) is not the highest among States – Kerala's is higher; its 60+ share is projected to rise from about 10% to 19% by 2036, not fall.

st.4: The replacement-level TFR of 2.1 was actually reached as early as NFHS-3 (2005-06).

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the medium-term objective was a TFR of 2.1 by 2010, not 2015; replacement level was reached only around NFHS-5 (2019-21), not NFHS-3.

st.2: Andhra Pradesh has 20.31 lakh Lakhpati Didis.

x: All three statements are correct: Streenidhi lends SHG members up to ₹1 lakh at 11%, AP has 20.31 lakh Lakhpati Didis, and Mega DSC-2025 recruited 15,941 teachers.

st.2: Interest-free loans to petty vendors
st.4: Insurance for unorganised workers

x: Not a statement set (matching): A-3, B-2, C-1, D-4 – Jagananna Chedodu gives ₹10,000 a year to tailors, rajakas and nayee brahmins, Jagananna Thodu interest-free loans to petty vendors, YSR Navodayam MSME debt restructuring, and Chandranna Bima insurance for unorganised workers.

st.3: The AP Socio-Economic Survey reports GSDP at 2011-12 prices.

x: All three statements are correct: the AP DES estimates GSDP in 9 sectors, the 2025-26 FAE is Rs 17.62 lakh crore, and the Survey still reports at 2011-12 prices.

st.1: Clause (2) of Article 38 was added by the 44th Amendment, 1978.

x: All three statements are correct: Article 38(2) came with the 44th Amendment (1978), Article 31C with the 25th (1971), and socialism aims at distributive justice.

st.2: The Rangarajan Expert Group was set up in 2012 and submitted its report in 2014.

x: All three statements are correct: Tendulkar (2005, report 2009) took a fresh look at poverty lines, and Rangarajan (2012, report 2014) was the last Planning Commission group on poverty.

st.2: NITI Aayog has no power to allocate plan funds to the States.

x: All three statements are correct: NITI Aayog is a think tank for bottom-up planning and cooperative-competitive federalism with no fund-allocating power, and Nehru admitted in 1958 that the Planning Commission had become a 'super-cabinet'.

st.2: The Governors of the States are not its members, though the Chief Ministers are.

x: All three statements are correct: all Union Cabinet Ministers have been NDC members since 1967, the Chief Ministers (not the Governors) are members, and its role has passed to NITI Aayog's Governing Council.

st.3: It adopted the Rolling Plan approach to reduce regional disparities.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct: the Fourth Plan expected exports to grow about 7 per cent a year, not 12; it adopted the Growth Centre approach, not the Rolling Plan (1978-80).

st.1: The RBI was to shift from being a facilitator to being a regulator.
st.4: Private buyers of more than 26% of a PSU's equity took over its ownership and management.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: the RBI was to move from regulator to facilitator, not the reverse; early disinvestment aimed mainly at raising resources, not at efficiency; ownership and management passed to private buyers of more than 51%, not 26%.

st.1: Now only about 5-6 industries are free of compulsory licensing.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: only about 5-6 industries still need a compulsory licence, the rest being free; MRTP asset limits were scrapped, not raised.

st.3: Urban local bodies must notify ceiling (maximum) property-tax rates to get the grants.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: the untied part cannot be used for salaries; urban local bodies must notify floor (baseline), not ceiling, property-tax rates.

st.2: Issue of municipal bonds is not one of the entry conditions.

x: All three statements are correct: audited accounts online and a timely State Finance Commission are entry conditions, while municipal bonds are not.

st.3: Allocation of funds to the States is one of its four mandate areas.
st.1: Credible plans are to be formulated at the national level and passed down progressively to the village level.

x: None of the statements is correct: plans are to be made at the village level and aggregated upwards, not passed down; NITI focuses on small, not large, enterprises; fund allocation is not one of its four mandate areas – monitoring and evaluation is.

st.2: MUDRA Ltd was set up on 18 March 2015 as a subsidiary of SIDBI.

x: All three statements are correct: MUDRA (Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency) Ltd is a SIDBI subsidiary set up on 18 March 2015, and PMMY gives collateral-free loans to non-corporate, non-farm micro and small units.

st.1: It was launched in April 2010 with 21 banks.

x: Neither statement is correct: UPI was launched in April 2016, not 2010 (the year of IMPS); it runs on the IMPS framework, not NEFT.

st.3: The Contingent Risk Buffer band of 4.5–7.5% was narrowed to 5.5–6.5% in 2025.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: the FY 2025-26 surplus of ₹2.86 lakh crore was a record, higher than FY25; the CRB band was widened from 5.5–6.5% to 4.5–7.5% in 2025, not narrowed.

st.1: India Post Payments Bank was set up in 2015.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: IPPB began in 2018 (India Post got its licence in 2015); tele-density for the quarter ending December 2025 was 91.74%, not 81.74%.

st.1: Education is on the State List of the Constitution.

x: Neither statement is correct: education is on the Concurrent List, not the State List; NEP 2020 targets public spending of 6% of GDP, not 4%.

st.3: Among these AIFIs, EXIM Bank is classed as a term-lending institution, while NABARD, NHB and SIDBI are refinance institutions.

x: All three statements are correct: the RBI regulates five AIFIs including NaBFID (added 2022); EXIM Bank is a term-lending institution, the others refinance institutions.

st.1: CRISIL was set up in 1987.

x: All three statements are correct: CRISIL dates from 1987, ICRA from 1991 (with Moody's) and CARE from 1993.

st.3: In December 2024, Konaseema had the highest and Tirupati the lowest district CD ratio.

x: All three statements are correct: AP's deposits were ₹6,08,834 crore and its CD ratio 157.40% (norm 60%); Konaseema had the highest and Tirupati the lowest district CD ratio.

st.3: NARCL aggregates the assets, while IDRCL resolves them.

x: All three statements are correct: PSBs hold a majority in NARCL, which aggregates the bad loans, while the majority-private IDRCL resolves them.

st.3: In a Credit Default Swap, the seller of protection pays the buyer upon default.

x: All three statements are correct: the crisis began in the US sub-prime market in July 2007, weak loans were securitised worldwide, and in a CDS the protection seller pays on default.

st.2: Those upgrades came from Morningstar DBRS, S&P and R&I.

x: All three statements are correct: cutting the deficit from 9.2% to 4.4% won three 2025 upgrades from Morningstar DBRS, S&P and R&I, and end-July 2026 deficit was 26.8% of target.

st.2: The States' own tax-GDP ratio alone is about 19.6%.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: about 19.6% is the combined Centre-plus-States ratio, not the States' alone; the World Bank's tipping point is 15%, not 20%.

st.2: The Income Declaration Scheme, 2016 (1 June – 30 September 2016) was launched soon after demonetisation.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: IDS 2016 (45% levy) came before demonetisation, which was followed by PMGKY; PMGKY carried a higher levy (50%), not a lower one.

st.1: The SEZ Act was enacted in 2000 and the SEZ policy was announced only in 2005.
st.4: Asia's first Export Processing Zone was set up at Santacruz (Mumbai) in 1965.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: the SEZ policy came first (1 April 2000) and the Act later (2005); the concept came from the EXIM Policy 1997-2002, not 1992-97; Asia's first EPZ was at Kandla, not Santacruz.

st.1: Land Tribunals under the Act are headed by the Revenue Divisional Officer (RDO).

x: All three statements are correct: Land Tribunals are headed by the RDO, benami transfers after 30 January 1970 are ignored, and only about 5 of 20 lakh surplus acres were taken over in Phase II.

st.3: It reserves at least one-half of the work for women.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: wages are to be paid within 15 days, not 30; the target for women is one-third, not one-half.

st.4: ISM 1.0 has 12 projects, most of them in Tamil Nadu.
st.1: It functions under the Department of Science and Technology.
st.2: It was approved in 2019 with an outlay of ₹76,000 crore.

x: None of the statements is correct: ISM works under the Digital India Corporation (MeitY), not DST; it was approved in 2021, not 2019; capital assistance is up to 50%, not 30%; most ISM 1.0 projects are in Gujarat, not Tamil Nadu.

st.1: YSR Navodayam (2019) provided interest-free loans to petty street vendors.
st.4: AP's MSME Policy 2026 withdraws the incentives for women-led MSMEs.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct: YSR Navodayam was a one-time restructuring of stressed MSME loans – interest-free loans to vendors is Jagananna Thodu; the MSME Policy 2026 adds, not withdraws, incentives for women-led MSMEs.

st.1: About 86.27 lakh students were enrolled in 2024-25.

x: Neither statement is correct: about 68.27 lakh, not 86.27 lakh, students were enrolled in 2024-25; the 2023-24 dropout rate was highest at the IX–XII level and lowest at I–V.

st.1: Andhra Pradesh's rice yield in 2022-23 was 2,844 kg/ha against the national 3,846 kg/ha.
st.2: In 2021-22, AP's maize yield of 3,392 kg/ha compared with a national average of 2,798 kg/ha.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: in 2022-23 AP's rice yield was 3,846 kg/ha against the national 2,844, not the reverse; the 2021-22 figures of 3,392 and 2,798 kg/ha are for rice, not maize; West Godavari, not Guntur, had the largest food-crop area.

st.3: Its unit of implementation is a cluster of about 5 Gram Panchayats.

x: All three statements are correct: APCNF covers about 10.20 lakh farmers on 4.89 lakh ha, targets 41 lakh farmers on 19 lakh ha by 2028-29, and works through clusters of about 5 Gram Panchayats.

st.4: PMFME supports large food processing units under the One District One Product approach.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: the Mega Food Park grant ceiling is ₹50 crore, not ₹100 crore; PMFME supports micro, not large, food-processing units.

st.2: They account for about 46% of imports.
st.1: They account for about 46% of GDP.

x: Only statement 4 is correct: MSMEs give about 30% of GDP, not 46%; their 46% share is of exports, not imports; women own about 20% of MSMEs, not 46%.

st.4: Orvakal (Kurnool) is a node of the Visakhapatnam-Chennai Industrial Corridor.
st.3: Kakinada is a node of the Chennai-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: the VCIC is funded by the ADB, not JICA; Kakinada is a node of the VCIC, not the Chennai-Bengaluru corridor; Orvakal is a node of the Hyderabad-Bengaluru corridor, not the VCIC.

st.1: NICDC, formerly DMICDC, functions under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry (DPIIT).

x: All three statements are correct: NICDC works under Commerce and Industry through DPIIT, NICDIT funds trunk infrastructure at Kopparthy, Krishnapatnam and Orvakal, and the programme covers 11 corridors.

st.1: The Asian Development Bank provides $215 million, i.e. 25.6% of the $840 million programme.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct: the $215 million (25.6%) comes from the Government of AP, not the ADB, which gives $625 million; the $125 million Policy-Based Loan is for ease of doing business and institutional reform, not trunk infrastructure.

st.3: Damaged food grains are barred as a feedstock for ethanol.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: the National Biofuel Coordination Committee is headed by the Minister of Petroleum and Natural Gas, not Agriculture; damaged food grains are a permitted feedstock.

st.1: Mercury is the smallest planet and has the shortest day of all the planets.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct: Mercury has the shortest year (88 days), but the shortest day belongs to Jupiter (about 10 hours); Venus, not Mercury, is the hottest planet, because of its dense CO2 atmosphere.

st.2: Its north–south extent is about 3,214 km and its east–west extent about 2,933 km.

x: All three statements are correct: India extends from 8°4'N to 37°6'N, about 3,214 km north–south and 2,933 km east–west, over 32,87,263 sq km.

st.1: Oceanic crust is about 30 km thick, while continental crust averages about 5 km.
st.4: The inner core remains solid because of its low temperature.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: oceanic crust is about 5 km and continental crust about 30 km thick, not the reverse; the outer core is liquid, not solid; the inner core stays solid because of immense pressure, not low temperature.

st.2: Dhinodhar and Mount Kenya are active volcanoes.
st.4: Mauna Loa is a composite volcano built of alternating layers of lava and ash.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: Dhinodhar and Mount Kenya are extinct, not active; a caldera is much larger than a crater, not the reverse; Mauna Loa is a shield volcano of fluid basalt, not a composite volcano.

st.1: About two-thirds of the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta lies in India.
st.3: Seven major deltas, all of them in Asia, account for about 57% of the world's sinking delta area.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: about two-thirds of the delta lies in Bangladesh, not India; the seven deltas include the Nile, Amazon and Mississippi, so not all are in Asia; the main causes of sinking are groundwater extraction and reduced silt, not sea-level rise and cyclones.

st.1: It has the lowest mean elevation of all continents, about 2,300 m.
st.2: India's IRS-1C made its first detailed and complete map in 1997.

x: Only statement 4 is correct: Antarctica has the highest, not lowest, mean elevation; its first complete map (1997) was made by Canada's RADARSAT-1, not India's IRS-1C; Maitri (1989) was India's second station – Bharati (2012) is the third.

st.1: As the Himalayas block cold, dry Central Asian air, north India is about 3–8°C colder than places on the same latitude.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct: the Himalayan barrier makes north India 3–8°C warmer, not colder; the SW monsoon air is fed by the low-level Somali Jet, not the Tropical Easterly Jet.

st.3: As per the IPCC, 2025 was about 1.43°C above the pre-industrial level.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct: India's IMD anomaly for 2025 (+0.28°C) was lower than 2024's (+0.65°C); the 1.43°C figure for 2025 is the WMO's, not the IPCC's.

st.1: During the SW monsoon, circulation in the Bay of Bengal and Arabian Sea is anticlockwise.
st.3: The West India Coastal Current flows southward (equatorward) from November to February.

x: Only statement 4 is correct: SW-monsoon circulation is clockwise, not anticlockwise; the EICC then flows northward, not southward; the WICC flows northward (poleward), not southward, from November to February.

st.2: Doddabetta is higher than Anaimudi.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: Anaimudi (2,695 m) is higher than Doddabetta (2,637 m), not the reverse; Kamet (7,756 m) is far higher than Doddabetta.

st.4: Pulicat is known for Siberian cranes.
st.3: Kolleru was declared a Ramsar site in 1981.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: Kolleru drains to the sea through the Upputeru, not the Budameru; it became a Ramsar site in 2002, not 1981; Pulicat is known for greater flamingos, not Siberian cranes.

st.1: The Andhra coastal plain is about 950 km long and about 200 km wide.
st.3: The Coromandel Coast runs from south of the Krishna to Kanyakumari and lies wholly in Tamil Nadu.

x: None of the statements is correct: the Andhra coastal plain is about 60 km wide, not 200; the Northern Circars lie north of the Krishna, not south; the Coromandel Coast includes the southern AP coast and is not wholly in Tamil Nadu.

st.3: NSTR lies in the Seshachalam hills.
st.1: The Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve (NSTR) was established in 1973 and covers about 3,728 sq km.

x: Only statement 4 is correct: NSTR was established in 1983, not 1973; its Telangana part is the Amrabad, not Kawal, Tiger Reserve; it lies in the Nallamala, not the Seshachalam, hills.

st.4: India's deadliest tornado struck Belda, Odisha, on 24 March 1998.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the IMD plains heat-wave threshold is 40 °C, not 45 °C; Belda, hit on 24 March 1998, is in West Bengal, not Odisha.

st.3: Seed modification is not a method of improving soil fertility.

x: All three statements are correct: IWMP began in 2009-10 and merged into PMKSY's Watershed Development Component in 2015-16; soil fertility is improved by rotation and manuring, not seed modification.

st.3: The Girijan Co-operative Corporation has its headquarters at Hyderabad.
st.1: TRIFED was set up in 1987 under the Companies Act, 1956.

x: None of the statements is correct: TRIFED was set up under the Multi-State Co-operative Societies Act, 1984, not the Companies Act; it works under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, not MoEFCC; the GCC's headquarters is at Visakhapatnam, not Hyderabad.

st.2: The Bhopal leak took place at the Union Carbide pesticide plant.

x: All three statements are correct: methyl isocyanate leaked from the Union Carbide pesticide plant in December 1984, and Fukushima (2011) followed an earthquake and tsunami.

st.1: The Indian Tsunami Early Warning Centre (ITEWC) is located at NIOT, Chennai.
st.2: ITEWC can detect a tsunamigenic earthquake within about 10 minutes but warns only the Indian coastline.

x: Only statement 4 is correct: ITEWC is at INCOIS, Hyderabad, not NIOT, Chennai; it can warn 25 Indian Ocean countries, not just India; World Tsunami Awareness Day is 5 November, not 26 December.

st.4: Sunderlal Bahuguna founded the Narmada Bachao Andolan, which opposed raising the height of Sardar Sarovar.
st.1: The Hirakud dam on the Mahanadi lies about 15 km from Cuttack.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: Hirakud is about 15 km from Sambalpur, not Cuttack; Madhya Pradesh, not Gujarat, gets the largest share (57%) of Sardar Sarovar's power; the NBA was founded by Medha Patkar, not Sunderlal Bahuguna.

st.1: India is the world's second largest user of groundwater, after China.
st.3: Groundwater over-exploitation is worst in Kerala, Haryana, Rajasthan and Delhi.

x: None of the statements is correct: India is the world's largest groundwater user, not second; PMKSY created about 24.61, not 42.61, million ha in ten years; over-exploitation is worst in Punjab, not Kerala, along with Haryana, Rajasthan and Delhi.

st.1: The Atomic Minerals Directorate reported 5.9 million tonnes of inferred lithium at Salal-Haimana in Reasi, Jammu and Kashmir.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: the 5.9 Mt Reasi lithium find was reported by the GSI, not the AMD; India is not the second largest miner of rare earths – China dominates.

st.2: Coal in Andhra Pradesh is found mainly in West Godavari district, not in Kadapa.

x: All three statements are correct: Kadapa holds barytes, uranium and asbestos; AP's coal is in West Godavari; Nellore gives mica and Prakasam black granite.

st.1: LPG, naphtha and anthracite are petroleum products.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct: anthracite is a coal, not a petroleum product; the first oil crisis came in 1973, not 1979.

st.2: Neyveli lignite belongs to the Tertiary coal of 15-60 million years.

x: All three statements are correct: Makum and Neyveli both hold Tertiary coal, and Neyveli has South-East Asia's first lignite-fired thermal power station.

st.1: Anthracite has the highest carbon content (80-95%) and in India occurs mainly in Jharkhand.
st.2: Lignite, or brown coal, has low moisture content.

x: Only statement 4 is correct: Indian anthracite occurs only in J&K, not mainly in Jharkhand; lignite has high, not low, moisture; Palana is in Rajasthan, not Gujarat.

st.2: Oak (temperate) tasar silk is mainly produced in Jharkhand.
st.1: Andhra Pradesh is the largest producer of mulberry silk in India.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: Karnataka, not AP, is the largest mulberry silk producer (AP is second); oak tasar comes mainly from Manipur, not Jharkhand; the Central Silk Board is at Bengaluru, not Hyderabad.

st.1: Andhra Pradesh ranks second in India in fish and shrimp production.

x: Neither statement is correct: AP ranks first, not second, in fish and shrimp production; after the remeasurement its coastline (1,053 km) is the third-longest, not second.

st.4: Steel is a capital good.
st.1: The Index of Industrial Production uses eight use-based classes.
st.2: Appliances fall under consumer non-durables.

x: None of the statements is correct: the IIP has six, not eight, use-based classes; appliances are consumer durables, not non-durables; there is no 'export goods' class; steel is a basic/primary good, not a capital good.

st.2: The Jalvahak scheme of 2024 covers NW-1, NW-2 and NW-3.
st.4: India's inland water transport cargo target is 500 MMT by 2030.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: Jal Marg Vikas is World Bank-supported, not ADB; Jalvahak covers NW-1, NW-2 and NW-16, not NW-3; the IWT cargo target is 200 MMT, not 500 MMT, by 2030.

st.3: V.O. Chidambaranar (Tuticorin), on the Gulf of Mannar south of Adam's Bridge, is the southernmost major port.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: Chennai is the oldest artificial port but not the deepest major port; Tuticorin lies north, not south, of Adam's Bridge.

st.4: Andhra Pradesh was an 'Aspirer' among coastal States in LEADS 2023.
st.3: Like the LPI, it ranks countries rather than Indian States.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: LEADS mixes perception and objective data, not only objective data; it ranks Indian States and UTs, while the LPI ranks countries; AP was an 'Achiever', not an 'Aspirer', among coastal States in LEADS 2023.

st.1: The official estimate of logistics cost for 2023-24 is 7.97% of GDP.

x: All three statements are correct: the official 2023-24 logistics cost is 7.97% of GDP, the 2022 policy targets the LPI top 25 by 2030, and India was 38th in LPI 2023.

st.3: Foxconn and Isuzu are located in Sri City (Tirupati).

x: All three statements are correct: JN Pharma City is at Parawada (Anakapalli), Brandix Apparel City at Atchutapuram, and Foxconn and Isuzu at Sri City.

st.3: APIIC is the nodal agency for industrial parks and SEZs in the State.

x: All three statements are correct: AP had 32 notified SEZs (July 2023), about 19 were operational in 2019 (4 pharma), and APIIC is the nodal agency.

st.2: Andhra Pradesh's sex ratio is lower than India's.

x: Neither statement is correct: AP's child sex ratio is higher than India's, not lower; AP's sex ratio (997) is higher than India's (943), not lower.

st.1: Scheduled Tribes formed 5.53% of the State's population in 1971.
st.4: Srikakulam district had the largest ST population.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: the ST share in 1971 was 4.39%, not 5.53% (the 2011 figure); Prakasam (23.19%), not SPS Nellore, had the highest SC share; Visakhapatnam, not Srikakulam, had the largest ST population.

st.3: Gor Boli, spoken by the Banjara/Sugali community of Andhra Pradesh, has not yet been included in the Eighth Schedule.

x: All three statements are correct: English has never been in the Eighth Schedule, Nepali is also an official language of Sikkim, and Gor Boli is still only a demand.

st.2: Pench Tiger Reserve spans Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra.

x: All three statements are correct: Melghat is in Maharashtra, Pench spans Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra, and Bandipur is in Karnataka.

st.4: Yanadis serve as protection watchers in NSTR.
st.2: NSTR is administered under the Tirupati circle on the NTCA core-buffer model.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: NSTR is not a biosphere reserve – AP's is Seshachalam; it is administered under the Srisailam, not Tirupati, circle; Chenchus, not Yanadis, serve as its protection watchers.

st.2: A UN brief of June 2026 said the 1.2°C tipping point for warm-water coral reefs has not yet been crossed.
st.1: The uninhabited Maldivian islets Tebua Tarawa and Abanuea were submerged in 1999.

x: None of the statements is correct: Tebua Tarawa and Abanuea are Kiribati, not Maldivian, islets; the June 2026 UN brief said the 1.2°C coral-reef tipping point has already been crossed; ocean acidity has risen about 30%, not 50%.

st.2: MSMEs account for about 46% of India's exports.

st.1: ULLAS stands for Understanding of Lifelong Learning for All in Society and targets adults aged 18 years and above.

st.3: A Sukanya Samriddhi account matures after 21 years.

st.1: CDSCO is an independent regulator that does not report to the Health Ministry.
st.3: India supplies about 40% of US generics and about 40% of the world's vaccines.

st.2: It is the 10th edition of the survey run by the Ministry of Jal Shakti.

st.1: Bela Gram Panchayat in Bhandara, Madhya Pradesh is India's first net-zero panchayat.

st.2: As per ISFR 2023, India's forest cover alone is 8,27,357 sq km, or 25.17% of its area.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: Van Mahotsav was started in 1950 by K.M. Munshi, not Nehru; 8,27,357 sq km (25.17%) is forest and tree cover together, not forest cover alone.

st.1: The UNFCCC's SB64 mid-year talks were held in Baku in June 2026.
st.4: UNCCD COP17 was held at Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, with the theme 'Restoring Land, Restoring Hope'.

st.3: APSCHE is India's first State Council of Higher Education, established on 11 November 1988.
st.1: Vidya Vahini was launched by the AICTE under its LMS–MOOCs initiative.

st.1: It was launched on the 12th National Handloom Day, 7 August 2026, in Mangalagiri constituency, Guntur district.
st.3: Weavers get ₹10,000 a month under NTR Pension Bharosa.

st.2: It is run by a consortium led by Bhavya Health Services Pvt Ltd, with SRIT India Pvt Ltd as a partner.

st.2: Srikalahasti is the next to adopt CVIRMS.

x: All three statements are correct: Tirupati was AP's first city with CVIRMS, Srikalahasti is next, and the Tirumala ICCC uses over 6,000 CCTV cameras.

st.2: Literacy in AP rose from 63% to 73% (2 April 2026).
st.1: Under Akshara Andhra, 24.7 lakh adults passed the National Achievement Survey (NAS) 2026.

st.2: Health, Medical and Family Welfare gets ₹27,719 crore.

st.3: The first of its ten Sutralu is Zero Poverty.

x: All three statements are correct: Swarna Andhra @2047 is aligned with Viksit Bharat @2047, targets $42,000 per capita and a $2.4 trillion economy, and its first Sutram is Zero Poverty.

st.1: It opposed the 56th GST Council decision to cut slabs from 4 to 2.

x: Neither statement is correct: the Assembly backed, not opposed, the cut from 4 slabs to 2; before GST AP had 17 indirect taxes and 13, not 17, cesses/surcharges.

st.3: The Dornala inscription records a well and sluice built by Velanga Parvata Nayani for the temple lands of Virupaksha at Hampi.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: Saka 1440 (1518 CE) falls in the 16th century, not the 15th; the inscription concerns the temple lands of Mallikarjuna Deva at Sriparvata (Srisailam), not Virupaksha at Hampi.

st.1: She was the first Indian woman to compete in the 400 m hurdles at the Olympics.
